field_definitions.Task: 实际研究、控制或预测的任务
field_definitions.Major finding: 作者摘要的一句话综合；详细贡献另见正文
field_definitions.Validation: 正文或已核对证据中的benchmark、实验任务及关键条件

papers.Task: Monitor/control traits and fine-tuning drift
papers.Major finding: Persona directions monitor and predict personality drift, supporting post-hoc suppression, preventative steering, and filtering risky training data.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Single-turn trait generation and training drift; includes many-shot context, not closed-loop agents. [Validation] Evil/sycophancy/hallucination; two models; prompt/fine-tuning drift, WildChat/LMSYS filtering, and MMLU capability controls.

papers.Task: Altruism, forgiveness, and expectations of others in games
papers.Major finding: Steering changes strategic choices and explanations, but wording can dissociate from strategy, and self-behavior directions partly differ from expectations of others.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Independent monetary/action responses in six games, not real multi-turn play or tool execution. [Validation] Qwen2.5-7B; six textual games (Dictator, Trust, etc.); actions/amounts, trait ratings, and activation projections measured together.

papers.Task: Assistant identity stability and multi-turn persona drift
papers.Major finding: The Assistant Axis characterizes the default assistant mode; constraining activations along it mitigates dialogue drift and persona jailbreaks.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Role extraction and simulated multi-turn drift/capping; coding controls are not tool-task scores. [Validation] 275 roles; vulnerable-user/self-reflective dialogue versus everyday/coding controls; persona jailbreaks and capability retention.

papers.Task: Effects of emotion concepts on preferences and misaligned behavior
papers.Major finding: Internal emotion concepts generalize across contexts and causally affect preferences, reward hacking, blackmail, and sycophancy.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Includes reward-hacking loops with actual code execution/unit-test feedback, plus preferences and simulated blackmail. [Validation] Claude Sonnet4.5; 171 emotions, 64 activity preferences; blackmail, 7 coding reward-hacking tasks, and sycophancy scenarios.

papers.Task: Behavior prediction and prompt control from self-reported personality
papers.Major finding: Alignment stabilizes self-reported personality, but self-reports predict behavior unreliably and persona prompting has weak or inconsistent behavioral effects.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Questionnaires and textual risk/bias/confidence tasks; sycophancy includes user disagreement, not tool actions. [Validation] 18 models; BFI/SRQ; CCT risk, IAT bias, confidence-based honesty, and sycophancy; base/instruct/persona controls.

papers.Task: Constitutional training for robust characters
papers.Major finding: Constitutional AI plus synthetic introspection yields characters more robust, coherent, and natural than prompting/steering.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Character training, single-turn preferences, and adversarial evaluation; self-interaction training includes ten-turn dialogue, without external tool loops. [Validation] Three models, 11 personas; revealed preferences, character-breaking prompts, coherence/realism, and five capability tests.

papers.Task: Big Five composition and dynamic dialogue-personality control
papers.Major finding: Training-free vector algebra approaches SFT-level personality control and supports context-dependent dynamic persona composition.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Static personality scores and Persona-Evolve multi-turn dynamic dialogue, not environmental actions. [Validation] PersonalityBench, contextualized BFI-44, 800 Persona-Evolve scenarios; multiple judges/human evaluation, trait composition, strength, and side effects.

papers.Task: Tracking persona-direction formation during pretraining
papers.Major finding: Very early pretraining persona directions already control final instruct models; geometry/semantics continue refining, and extraction paradigms emphasize different facets.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Trait-text extraction/steering across pretraining checkpoints; dialogue is an extraction paradigm, not a closed-loop agent. [Validation] 17 OLMo3-7B checkpoints plus SFT/DPO/RLVR; four traits; Apertus8B and description/dialogue/narration checks.

papers.Task: Cross-persona preference readout and causal control
papers.Major finding: Assistant-trained preference probes transfer across personas, even predicting and controlling an evil character with opposing preferences.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Pairwise task preferences, role-conditioned readout, and open generation; selected tasks are not actually executed. [Validation] Cross-topic choices on Gemma3-27B/Qwen3.5-122B; Gemma causal steering, random-direction and held-topic controls.

papers.Task: Causal links between representational manifolds and output-behavior paths
papers.Major finding: Steering along activation manifolds stays closer to natural behavior manifolds than straight interpolation; reverse optimization recovers their curvature.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Language sequences/graph ICL and video world-model state paths, without action-feedback control loops. [Validation] Weekday/month/alphabet/age tasks, synthetic graph ICL, MountainCar visual world model; manifold versus linear paths.

papers.Task: Perspective diversity and dialogue structure in reasoning traces
papers.Major finding: Effective reasoning accompanies internal multiperspective dialogue; accuracy-rewarded training also increases conversational behavior.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Internal dialogue in long CoT and Countdown/RL reasoning, not separate interacting agents or tool loops. [Validation] DeepSeek-R1/QwQ traces; R1-Distill SAE intervention on 1,024 Countdown questions; controlled RL on two 3B models.

papers.Task: Dissociation and composition of risk self-report and choice channels
papers.Major finding: Nearly orthogonal directions separately control self-report and risk choices; composition aligns or opposes the channels.
papers.Validation: [Setting] CCT/BART and questionnaires read valid-answer-token probabilities, not continuous risk-taking or tool execution. [Validation] Four models, nine extraction methods; CCT/BART and BFI/DOSPERT; token likelihoods, dose/random-direction/surface controls.

papers.Task: Separating false agreement, genuine agreement, and flattery
papers.Major finding: Sycophantic agreement, genuine agreement, and flattery have distinct linear representations that can be amplified or suppressed separately.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Single-turn factual/praise control plus SYCON multi-turn user pressure, not tool actions. [Validation] Arithmetic/factual tasks controlling correctness and praise; multiple models; SycophancyEval, SYCON-Bench, and subspace-removal controls.

papers.Task: Evaluating agents’ discovery of hidden model behaviors
papers.Major finding: Standalone tool utility does not directly become auditing-agent gains; scaffolded black-box calls remain the best investigation tools.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Investigation agents iteratively query audited models with tools; steering affects the target, not investigator. [Validation] 56 hidden-behavior models, 14 behaviors, 13 tool configurations; fixed25,000-output-token budget, 16 repeats, implantation/anti-confession controls.

papers.Task: Jointly predicting many-shot ICL and steering effects
papers.Major finding: A Bayesian model jointly predicts both interventions; approximate addition in log-belief space explains sigmoid responses and transition boundaries.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Many-shot demonstrations are long input, with Yes/No-probability endpoints, not environmental feedback or long-horizon action. [Validation] Five persona types; shot/steering-strength sweeps and held-out strength prediction; additional concepts including sentiment.

papers.Task: Identifying narrow fine-tuning objectives from activation differences
papers.Major finding: Narrow fine-tuning leaves decodable artifacts in activations on unrelated text, substantially helping agents identify training objectives.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Offline fine-tuning-difference readouts/text injection; interpretability agents separately identify training domains through model-query tools. [Validation] 33 organisms, 1B–32B; false facts/EM/subliminal/taboo; 10,000 unrelated web texts, black-box and pretraining-data-mixing controls.

papers.Task: Weight-space behavioral control and fine-tuning-drift repair
papers.Major finding: Contrastive weight directions generally control behavior across distributions better than tested activation directions, partly repairing fine-tuning-induced sycophancy/refusal degradation.
papers.Validation: [Setting] QA/advice/evil-MCQA and repair after mathematics training, not environmental execution or multi-turn agents. [Validation] TruthfulQA/TriviaQA, evil-MCQA; repair after GCD/GSM8K fine-tuning, jointly measuring task gains/general capability.

papers.Task: Tracking trait distillation through semantically unrelated data
papers.Major finding: Students learn teacher-aligned steering vectors from unrelated numeric outputs; transferable traits depend on directional effects and optimization.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Numeric teacher distillation, animal-preference QA, and directional interventions, not agent traces. [Validation] Two open models; numeric sequences, 16 animal preferences, direction replacement/ablation, and Adam–SGD controls.

papers.Task: User-trait simulation and agent-interaction stress tests
papers.Major finding: Changing only simulated users’ traits lowers frontier-agent performance on τ-Trait by2%–30% on average.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Persona vectors steer user simulators; tested agents execute database/tool tasks, while BFCL uses AST matching. [Validation] Four-domain τ-Trait (airline/retail/telecom/telemedicine), BFCL multi-turn tool calls; human realism/composed-trait evaluation.

papers.Task: Localizing and controlling distributed behavior in long responses
papers.Major finding: Generative causal mediation localizes control components from long responses; sparse head intervention outperforms correlation-probe localization.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Head mediation/steering on single-turn complete responses; long responses are not long-horizon agent tasks. [Validation] Three models; refusal, sycophancy, prose-to-poetry; held-out long responses scored for target behavior, relevance, and fluency.

papers.Task: Distilling prompt interventions and dynamically regulating steering
papers.Major finding: Prompt-intervention strength varies by token; PSR mimics this pattern and improves control, especially under high-coherence constraints.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Persona Vectors/IFEval/AxBench responses; token-wise coefficients do not establish multi-step agent control. [Validation] Persona Vectors, IFEval, AxBench; multiple models; control–coherence trade-offs versus prompting/fixed steering.

papers.Task: Training-free pruning to extract persona subnetworks
papers.Major finding: A little calibration data localizes persona-specific subnetworks; contrastive pruning strengthens separation/control of opposing personas.
papers.Validation: [Setting] MBTI/AI Persona and scripted RoleAgentBench multiple-choice/dialogue, not actual multi-agent tool tasks. [Validation] MBTI, AI persona, RoleAgentBench; MMLU/HellaSwag retention, sparsity, and module-restoration ablations.

papers.Task: Localizing style heads for persona control
papers.Major finding: A few Style Modulation Heads support persona control in main models; localized intervention reduces coherence degradation from residual steering.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Multi-trait text generation and per-head interventions/ablations, without tool feedback or long-term persona measurement. [Validation] Traits and positive/negative strength sweeps; per-head interventions/ablations, trait–coherence frontiers, and capability controls.

papers.Task: Value-intensity evaluation and multi-value control
papers.Major finding: Unified value extraction, calibrated scoring, and control reveal directional asymmetries and multi-value composition patterns across ten models.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Value-intensity responses, OpinionQA, and multi-value prompt composition, not activation-based agent control. [Validation] Ten models×four value theories; VIDB ranking anchors, human evaluation, OpinionQA group preferences, and composition.

papers.Task: Comparing PPS and inoculation defense mechanisms
papers.Major finding: PPS reverses gradient pressure along trait axes and reduces existing evilness; IP shows different gradient patterns and struggles to remove existing traits.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Defensive fine-tuning and gradient/trait-projection experiments, with trait-text endpoints rather than agent execution. [Validation] Qwen2.5-7B evilness narrow fine-tuning; initial trait strengths, gradient-projection/sign interventions, and cross-trait controls.

papers.Task: Explain and constrain out-of-domain generalization from narrow-domain fine-tuning
papers.Major finding: Shared chat-template tokens can carry fine-tuned behavior out of domain; TReFT regularization reduces spillover while preserving within-domain learning.
papers.Validation: [Setting] EM QA and search_info call-string detection, with preset tool returns; no real retrieval feedback loop. [Validation] Multiple models/EM datasets; prefix perturbation/patching; extensions to abstention, tool calls, refusal, and short-answer length.

papers.Task: Predict post-reasoning behavior and control generation paths
papers.Major finding: Features predicting future behavior differ from detectors of generated behavior; FPCG selects sentences prospectively to control behavior while largely preserving output quality.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Candidate continuations/future-behavior probabilities at CoT sentence boundaries; includes contextual decisions but no live tool-action traces. [Validation] Four reasoning-model types, six binary behaviors, repeated sentence-boundary continuations, held-out probes, and activation-steering controls.

papers.Task: Shape and bind assistant personas from pretraining
papers.Major finding: Value reflections introduced from token zero and bound during post-training improve value adherence/out-of-domain dilemmas more than final-stage-only exposure.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Pretraining/SFT, value-choice probabilities, and jailbreak generation; long training is not long-horizon agent execution. [Validation] Self-trained1.7B/100B-token and3B/500B-token models; constitutions, jailbreaks, AI-risk dilemmas, and persona-binding controls.

papers.Task: Internal emotion interventions and stage-specific agent-behavior analysis
papers.Major finding: Emotion–behavior relationships are non-monotonic; selected emotions improve capabilities/safety and systematically change multi-step agent performance.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Beyond single-turn capability tasks, planner–decider–executor tool execution/replanning; not production long coding traces. [Validation] Logic/code/math/creativity/safety; HotpotQA, Scientific, GAIA; module-specific interventions.

papers.Task: Predict narrow-domain EM generalization and directional transfer
papers.Major finding: EM generalization depends on data/format: pretraining representation distances predict effects, and no malicious direction is universal across tested EM models.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Independent post-EM question generation, format/prompt perturbations; not continuous agent actions. [Validation] Twelve model–data settings; training-format changes, cross-EM direction ablation, random suffixes/paraphrases.

papers.Task: Read and causally edit the model's user beliefs
papers.Major finding: BSD extracts and writes compact user representations; changing inferred intent for fixed requests changes refusal, with shared geometry across models.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Offline natural-dialogue histories; endpoints are user-attribute MCQs/refusal interventions, not online tools. [Validation] Three models,13 attributes, approximately58k natural dialogues; held-out reads/writes, fixed harmful requests, random-write-map/cross-model controls.

papers.Task: Separate shared sentiment axes from usage residuals
papers.Major finding: Beyond robust shared sentiment directions, low-dimensional tone/audience structure remains; residual-tone steering changes expression while preserving polarity.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Event-text tone/audience readout, erasure, and single-turn generation; not multi-step agents. [Validation]221 event skeletons/3,536 texts; Llama/Mistral/Gemma; event-based splits, target/random erasure, and blind Llama-generation evaluation.

papers.Task: Big Five control and cross-trait interference
papers.Major finding: Cross-trait coupling persists after removing linear directional overlap, and forced orthogonality may weaken control.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Interview-style BFI generation measures trait coupling; no closed-loop actions reported, independent multi-turn progression unverified. [Validation] LLaMA-3-8B/Ministral-8B; BFI interviews; six geometric conditions; target/off-target traits and fluency.

papers.Task: Predict behavioral side effects of activation steering
papers.Major finding: Side effects are widespread, structured, and asymmetric; unsteered representations predict their signs better than similarity baselines.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Behavioral-coupling matrices from generated text in six contexts; context types are not multi-turn environment tasks. [Validation] Three models×67 behaviors, six contexts; cross-effect matrices, held-source/target forecasts, multi-behavior ratings.

papers.Task: Budget-constrained rank1 layer/strength search
papers.Major finding: Geometry guidance reduces search trials by39.8% on average; cross-context direction heterogeneity correlates with search difficulty and performance limits.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Budgeted layer/strength search across prompts; search trials are not agent actions. [Validation] Three model families×20 concepts; separate extraction/evaluation questions; layer/coefficient search; trials to95% of best-found utility.

papers.Task: Reuse role vectors to reduce sycophancy
papers.Major finding: Critical-role vectors not extracted for sycophancy approach dedicated CAA effects despite low cosine similarity.
papers.Validation: [Setting] PhilPapers option logits and16 factual probes; role vectors do not directly execute agent tasks. [Validation] Gemma2-27B/Qwen3-32B; counterbalanced PhilPapers, separate tuning split,16 factual probes.

papers.Task: Choose activation sources for steering-signal extraction
papers.Major finding: With downstream intervention fixed, execution-boundary states provide stronger signals than text already expressing the behavior; tail subtraction improves them further.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Single-turn tasks comparing source contexts/readout positions; execution boundary means generation boundary, not tool execution. [Validation] Three instruct models; entity/persona-style/refusal/nonsense tasks, held-out general questions, controlled source/readout positions.

papers.Task: Evaluate persona drift in long-horizon coding agents
papers.Major finding: Real agent sessions exhibit early-onset, cross-provider drift; compaction does not reliably reset it, and anchor recovery includes generic register-reset effects.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Real long coding/tool traces as corpus; controls mainly use snapshot-branch probes/format, not full-task steering. [Validation] ContextEcho:25 identity probes,57 real coding sessions,23-model representative-session panel; snapshot probing and compaction/placebo controls.

papers.Task: Steering-vector identifiability and output equivalence
papers.Major finding: Under single-layer white-box local linearity, different directions can have equivalent outputs, preventing unique identification from behavioral tests.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Single-layer linearization theory and trait/logit generation controls; no agent-trace validation. [Validation] Llama3.1-8B/Qwen2.5-3B, five traits; orthogonal perturbations, mean-difference/PCA, strengths/prompt distributions, classifiers/logits.

papers.Task: Empathy-direction decodability and causal control
papers.Major finding: Decodable empathy does not guarantee reliable control: Resonance partly changes automatic scores; Recognition is also limited by measurement resolution.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Empathy readout/addition/ablation in emotional-support answers; not long-term human dialogue or tool execution. [Validation] Three instruct models, EPITOME Recognition/Resonance, two LLM judges plus classifiers, emotional/neutral positive controls, addition/ablation.

papers.Task: Maintain and restore persistent-agent identity
papers.Major finding: Persona information remaining in history does not guarantee enacted identity; lost system anchors and dialogue context jointly affect identity reversion.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Persistent-harness heartbeat/identity-restoration tests with historical tool records; no tool-task success evaluation. [Validation] Claude Opus4.5 persistent agent; anchor retention/loss/restoration, heartbeat/human interaction;46 anchored probes without failure.

papers.Task: Preserve coherence in multi-turn persona steering
papers.Major finding: GCAD uses attention contributions and tokenwise gating to preserve trait control while sharply reducing coherence degradation under persistent KV cache.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Fifteen traits×ten-turn persistent-KV-cache dialogue; no tool actions or environmental feedback. [Validation] Qwen2.5-7B/Llama3.1-8B;60 conversations per trait/condition, trait/coherence ratings.

papers.Task: Compare controllability across target behaviors
papers.Major finding: Steering depends on behavior category; trait strength follows an inverted-U coefficient curve, while vector separation fails to predict success.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Independent generation for50 behaviors at a fixed layer, with coefficient/data-size sweeps; not agent tasks. [Validation] Llama3.1-8B L15; role/trait/misalignment/style/public-figure imitation; coefficient, vector, and sample-size sweeps.

papers.Task: Compare safety across persona-induction methods
papers.Major finding: Persona safety rankings change with induction method and architecture; a prosocial persona safe under prompting can be most dangerous under activation steering.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Harmful-request responses/reasoning traces after persona induction; not tool-agent safety. [Validation] Four standard plus two reasoning models; system/few-shot/CAA, Study1's5,568 judged conditions, coefficient/persona-strength matching.

papers.Task: Identify sources of steering interference
papers.Major finding: Most interference is asymmetric and reflects model fallback tendencies under perturbation; matched-norm random pushes yield similar off-target rankings.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Twenty-four-behavior text cross-interference, random pushes, ten-model replication; not long-horizon control. [Validation] Ten instruct models×24 behaviors; generated-text judges, matched-norm random directions, leave-one-behavior-out prediction/cross-model replication.

papers.Task: Inference-time VLM jailbreak defense with benign-capability preservation
papers.Major finding: Authors report that adaptive steering in low-dimensional safety subspaces reduces jailbreak success while maintaining or improving benign-task performance.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Image/text jailbreak inputs→single generation; early-token adaptive steering, no environmental action loop. [Validation] LLaVA/MiniGPT4/Qwen2.5-VL; image perturbation/text-in-image attacks, adaptive attacks, MM-Vet benign capability.

papers.Task: Deconfound personality/emotion/topic/truthfulness directions for stable control
papers.Major finding: Contrastive-covariance subspaces filter confounds, improve tested concept control/output quality, and sustain control over20-turn dialogue.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Single-turn generation plus20-turn persistent-KV-cache dialogue; not tool agents. [Validation] Three dense models; AxBench, BIG5/NPTI, Emotion, TruthfulQA; topic-bias oracle controls;23 raters/296 generations.

papers.Task: Long-horizon multi-agent task/role stability, state maintenance, tool permissions, and embodied cooperation
papers.Major finding: ATLAS combines task–role–state spectral kernels with dynamic memory interventions, improving collaboration and reducing drift in memory, state, tool, and embodied stress tests.
papers.Validation: [Setting] Long-dialogue memory and closed-loop multi-agent tasks; AMemGym30–100 turns/episode, ALARA environments, LIBERO actions. [Validation] EverMemBench2,400 QA; AMemGym1,000 episodes; ToolACE500 two-to-six-call chains, AST/arguments; ALARA115 tasks; LIBERO10 tasks×50 rollouts×three seeds.
